title: Fail-closed pre-push review with round budgets
summary: The pre-push review stops being advisory. `--warn-only` is removed, so `osf review run` now fails a push on a kept must-fix or should-fix finding, and on a review that could not run. Two separate round budgets, kept in the journal state outside the worktree and keyed by worktree path, let a push through after `in_sandbox_rounds` failed finding rounds, while a could-not-run streak stops the push with a message instead of ever becoming a pass. A credential preflight decides a reviewer with no key and no login file before any worker starts, the work item can now come from `OSF_WORK_ITEM`, osf's own untracked `.osf/` output is excluded from changeset risk, and login-file values join the secret scrub list. The pull-request reduce step applies the same kept-finding rule but never spends the budget.

lanes.subtitle: moon task in the builder's workspace
lanes.summary: The moon `review` task that runs before a push, and the work item it feeds the review.

lanes.label: osf CLI
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf
lanes.summary: The command surface: argument parsing, exit-code decision, config loading and the review run itself.

lanes.label: Review engine
lanes.subtitle: reviewers, lenses, reducer
lanes.summary: Reviewer roster and credential preflight, the per-lens runs, and the deterministic reducer that decides the verdict.

lanes.subtitle: outside the worktree

nodes.label: moon review task
nodes.subtitle: osf review run --if-enabled --work-item ...
nodes.summary: The pre-push task. It loses `--warn-only`, gains `--work-item .osf/out/work-item.txt`, and drops its declared output so the review runs on every push rather than being served from a cache that cannot see `OSF_WORK_ITEM`.

nodes.label: work item body
nodes.subtitle: .osf/out/work-item.txt or OSF_WORK_ITEM
nodes.summary: The spec text the review reads. It can now arrive as a file, as the environment variable `OSF_WORK_ITEM`, or from the linked issue; a missing file falls back to the environment, any other read error stays an error.

nodes.label: review run
nodes.subtitle: review_run_exit_code
nodes.summary: Runs the review and turns its outcome into an exit code. `--warn-only` is gone; the code is now the base verdict, raised to 1 by a kept must-fix or should-fix finding, then passed through the round budget.

nodes.label: finish_review
nodes.subtitle: verdict + kept findings -> exit code
nodes.summary: Prints the lines, writes SARIF, posts when asked, then computes the base code from the verdict and the kept findings. Only the pre-push path counts rounds; the reduce path returns the base code unchanged.

nodes.label: review_base / round_kind
nodes.subtitle: Pass+blocking -> 1, Findings round
nodes.summary: Two small pure functions that split the decision: the exit code before any budget, and which budget a round spends. A could-not-run verdict always spends the could-not-run budget, even when another lens kept a finding.

nodes.label: review reduce
nodes.subtitle: review_reduce_exit_code
nodes.summary: The pull-request side. It applies the same kept-finding rule but passes `count_rounds = false`, so repeated reduce calls stay failures and never turn into a budget pass.

nodes.label: [review] config
nodes.subtitle: in_sandbox_rounds, could_not_run_rounds
nodes.summary: Two new positive-integer settings, three each by default, refused at zero and named in the error. The whole-run timeout default drops from 2700 to 1800 seconds, and the repository's own `osf.toml` sets concurrency 16 and the 1800-second limit.

nodes.label: review_run::run
nodes.subtitle: setup, reviewers, reduce
nodes.summary: The review engine. It now runs the credential preflight before starting a worker, and exposes the round-budget API the CLI calls.

nodes.label: credential preflight
nodes.subtitle: Reviewer::missing_credentials
nodes.summary: Decides, before any process starts, that a reviewer with no non-empty credential variable and no existing login file cannot answer. A templated reviewer is exempt, and an unknown home is not treated as absent. The reviewer is recorded as could-not-run for every lens with no worker started.

nodes.label: reviewer roster
nodes.subtitle: Reviewer { templated, credential_env, login_paths }
nodes.summary: The roster entry gains a `templated` flag, set when a launch template supplied the command, so a template that carries its own authentication is not judged by the preflight.

nodes.label: reducer verdict
nodes.subtitle: Pass / Fail / CouldNotRun
nodes.summary: The deterministic reducer that decides the verdict and keeps findings. Unchanged, but its verdict now selects which round budget a run spends.

nodes.label: secret scrub list
nodes.subtitle: held() + login_values()
nodes.summary: The values removed from reviewer output now include every string leaf of the agents' JSON login files, so a provider key kept in opencode's or codex's auth file is scrubbed like an environment secret.

nodes.label: changeset risk
nodes.subtitle: untracked .osf/ excluded
nodes.summary: Untracked files under `.osf/` are filtered out of the changed-file set, so osf's own review output cannot raise the risk tier or change which lenses the next round selects.

nodes.label: RoundCounts
nodes.subtitle: review-rounds/<hash>.json
nodes.summary: Two counters, `review` and `could_not_run`, serialized to the journal state directory under a hash of the canonical worktree path. Each develop run has its own count, and the builder cannot edit it from the worktree.

nodes.label: round_allows_push
nodes.subtitle: Pass clears, Findings increments, CouldNotRun blocks
nodes.summary: Applies the budget. A pass clears the counts. A findings round increments and allows the push once past the limit. A could-not-run round increments and, past its own limit, returns an error naming the block rather than allowing the push.

edges.label: osf review run
edges.summary: The task invokes the CLI with the work-item path and no warn-only flag.

edges.label: --work-item
edges.summary: The task names the file the caller writes before the push.

edges.label: body or OSF_WORK_ITEM
edges.summary: The review context reads the work item, falling back to the environment when the file is missing.
The command runs the review engine and hands its outcome to finish_review.

edges.label: count_rounds = true
edges.summary: The pre-push path is the only caller that spends the round budget.

edges.label: count_rounds = false
edges.summary: The pull-request path applies the kept-finding rule but never touches the budget.
The base exit code and the round kind are computed from the verdict and the kept findings.

edges.label: round limits
edges.summary: The two limits are read from the trusted config root before the budget is applied.

edges.label: may this push go?
edges.summary: The connection the change is really about: the review's verdict now asks the journal-state budget whether the push may proceed.

edges.label: load / save / clear
edges.summary: The budget loads the per-worktree counters, increments the one its round kind names, and saves them back.

edges.label: before any worker
edges.summary: Each reviewer is judged for credentials before its worker starts, so a missing key is a deterministic could-not-run rather than a timeout.

edges.label: credential_env, login_paths, templated
edges.summary: The preflight reads the roster entry's credential variables, login paths and template flag.
The engine reduces the saved answers to a verdict and kept findings.

edges.label: tier and signals
edges.summary: Setup assesses the change to pick lenses; the assessment no longer counts untracked `.osf/` output.

edges.label: held values
edges.summary: Reviewer output is scrubbed against the held values, which now include login-file leaves.

views.title: The pre-push review gate
views.summary: How a push is now decided: the moon task runs the review, the CLI turns the verdict and kept findings into a base code, and the journal-state budget decides whether that code stops the push.

views.title: Review engine internals
views.summary: Inside the review run: the credential preflight against the roster, the risk assessment that selects lenses, the reducer, and the scrub list.
